question.problem:
Given that $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ is the standard Hermitian inner product over $C,$ find $⟨2a+3b,\,c⟩$ if 

$\,$ $⟨c,a⟩=2-\text{i}\,$ and $\,⟨b,c⟩=1+2\text{i}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties. 

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

First, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ is linear in the first argument: 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨2a+3b,\,c⟩ & =⟨2a,c⟩+⟨3b,c⟩ \\  & =2⟨a,c⟩+3⟨b,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry: 

$$
\begin{aligned}2⟨a,c⟩+3⟨b,c⟩ & =2\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}+3⟨b,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $⟨c,a⟩$ and $⟨b,c⟩:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}+3⟨b,c⟩ & =2(\overset{―}{2-\text{i}})+3(1+2\text{i}) \\  & =2(2+\text{i})+3(1+2\text{i}) \\  & =4+2\text{i}+3+6\text{i} \\  & =7+8\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
